blurb: In the fragment form of a `commons` or `context` (the header with no braces), the `uses` clauses come straight after the header, before any `type` or `fn`. Move the `uses` line up. `consumes` and `exports` clauses follow the same rule, as `bynk.parse.consumes_after_decls` and `bynk.parse.exports_after_decls`: `consumes` after the `uses` lines, `exports` after the `consumes` lines.
example:
commons demo
type Id = String
uses util              // ✗ a declaration comes first

commons demo
uses util              // ✓ clauses straight after the header
type Id = String
